title: Covenant-condition view comes to the same: living love-working faith required
source_text: XXIII. Eodem vero redit sententia eorum qui docent fidem nos justificare ut est foederis gratiae conditio. Etenim in eo mens eorum alia non est, quam Deum, ut nos pro justis habeat, & propter Christum ad vitam & gloriam aeternam acceptet, non aliud in Evangelio a nobis exigere, quam ut Christo fide viva & per dilectionem operante adhaereamus; & sub hac, non vero alia conditione, salutem & remissionem peccatorum nostrorum, Evangelii verbo nobis offeri & promitti: atque hanc esse rationem cur in Scriptura fide justificari dicimur.
pass_a_gloss: But the view of those who teach that faith justifies us as it is the condition of the covenant of grace comes to the same thing. For in that their mind is nothing other than that God, in order to hold us as just and accept us for Christ's sake to eternal life and glory, requires nothing else of us in the Gospel than that we cling to Christ with living faith working through love; and that under this condition—not another—salvation and the remission of our sins are offered and promised to us by the word of the Gospel: and that this is the reason why in Scripture we are said to be justified by faith.
pass_b_english: Faith-as-covenant-condition means the same: cling to Christ with living love-working faith.
Under that—not another—condition the gospel promises salvation and remission.

lemmas.gloss: condition of the covenant of grace

choices.why: Gospel's required condition is living faith.
